<b>Начало гена β-глобина.</b> Верхние ря: The start of the β-globin gene. The top rows are the two DNA strands, below them is the mRNA (U instead of T), and under it the protein: the ribosome reads each three-nucleotide codon as one amino acid according to the genetic code. The sequence here encodes Met-Val-His-Leu-Thr-Pro-Glu-Glu-Lys-Ser-Ala-Val-Thr… Choose a mutation type and the protein will be recalculated using the real genetic code.
<b>Молчащая мутация</b>: CTG → CTC, но о: Silent mutation: CTG → CTC, but both codons mean leucine — the code is degenerate (most amino acids have several codons, and the third letter often doesn’t matter). The protein is unchanged.
<b>Миссенс-мутация</b>: GAG → GTG в 6-м: Missense mutation: GAG → GTG in codon 6 (counting after the methionine, which is later cleaved off): glutamate is replaced by valine. This is hemoglobin S, the cause of sickle cell anemia. One letter out of 3 billion — and a hydrophilic residue on the protein surface becomes a hydrophobic “sticky” patch (see the “Sickle cells” mode).
<b>Нонсенс-мутация</b>: GAG → TAG — кодо: Nonsense mutation: GAG → TAG — the glutamate codon has become a stop codon. The ribosome terminates the protein early, and the short fragment is degraded (often already at the mRNA level). This is how many β⁰-thalassemias arise: there is no β-globin at all.
<b>Сдвиг рамки считывания</b>: выпал оди: Reading frame shift: a single nucleotide is deleted, and all the following codons are read out of frame — an entirely different protein follows until a stop codon happens to turn up. Insertions and deletions that are multiples of three do not shift the frame.
<b>Серповидноклеточная анемия</b> (HbSS: Sickle cell anemia (HbSS — both copies of the gene are mutant). While oxygen is plentiful, the red blood cells are normal. When hemoglobin S gives up its oxygen, the “sticky” valine of one molecule binds to a neighboring one — hemoglobin polymerizes into long, rigid fibers, and the cell turns into a sickle. Sickle cells get stuck in capillaries (pain, organ infarctions) and are rapidly destroyed (anemia).
<b>Носитель</b> (HbAS): половина гемогло: Carrier (HbAS): half of the hemoglobin is normal, and sickling occurs only under severe hypoxia (high altitude, strenuous exertion). Carrier status (sickle cell trait) protects against severe malaria — which is why the mutation is so common in Africa, India and the Mediterranean.
<b>Норма</b> (HbAA): эритроциты сохраняю: Normal (HbAA): red blood cells keep their biconcave disk shape at any level of oxygen saturation.
<b>Фосфорилирование</b>: протеинкиназа (: Phosphorylation: a protein kinase (orange) transfers a phosphate from ATP to the OH group of serine, threonine or tyrosine. The protein’s charge and shape change — this is the cell’s main “switch”: it turns enzymes (glycogen phosphorylase, glycogen synthase), receptors and channels on and off. Phosphatases remove the phosphate again.
<b>Гликозилирование</b> в ЭПС и аппарате: Glycosylation in the ER and Golgi apparatus: sugar chains are attached to asparagine (N-linked) or serine/threonine (O-linked). This is how membrane and secreted proteins are tagged: ABO blood group antigens, mucins of mucus, hormones (TSH, LH). Non-enzymatic attachment of glucose is glycation: HbA1c reflects blood sugar over the past 3 months.
<b>Частичный протеолиз</b>: проинсулин (: Partial proteolysis: proinsulin (a single chain) is cleaved in the secretory granules of β-cells — the C-peptide (gray) is removed, while chains A and B remain linked by disulfide bridges: this is insulin. Blood C-peptide levels show how much insulin the body is producing itself. Digestive enzymes (trypsinogen → trypsin), clotting factors and many hormones are activated in the same way.
<b>Гидроксилирование пролина и лизина</b: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine in collagen: prolyl hydroxylase requires vitamin C. Hydroxyproline stabilizes the collagen triple helix. Without vitamin C, collagen is weak — scurvy: bleeding gums, loss of teeth, poor wound healing.
<b>γ-Карбоксилирование</b> глутамата в ф: γ-Carboxylation of glutamate in clotting factors II, VII, IX and X (and in osteocalcin): a second carboxyl group converts glutamate into Gla, which binds Ca²⁺ — without it the factors cannot attach to platelet membranes. The enzyme requires vitamin K; warfarin blocks its regeneration — and that is how it thins the blood.
<b>Убиквитин</b> (зелёные шарики) — метк: Ubiquitin (green beads) is a “destroy me” tag: enzymes attach a chain of several ubiquitins to a lysine of the protein, and the proteasome (purple barrel) cuts it into short peptides. This is how the cell removes damaged and unneeded proteins and regulates the cell cycle. The proteasome inhibitor bortezomib is used to treat multiple myeloma.
Одна буква в ДНК может ничего не изменит: A single letter in DNA may change nothing — or turn a red blood cell into a sickle. And once a protein is assembled, it is still being finished: tagged, cut and sent for destruction.

Mutations

Gene (point) mutations: base substitutions — transitions (purine ↔ purine) and transversions; by their consequences — silent, missense, nonsense; insertions and deletions — with or without a frameshift. There are also mutations in regulatory regions and splice sites (many β⁺-thalassemias). Chromosomal mutations — deletions, duplications, inversions, translocations; genomic mutations — a change in chromosome number (trisomy 21).

Causes and defenses

Replication errors, spontaneous deamination and depurination, UV light (thymine dimers), ionizing radiation, chemical mutagens. Repair: direct reversal, excision repair (base and nucleotide excision — a defect causes xeroderma pigmentosum), mismatch repair (defect — Lynch syndrome). See the “DNA” topic.

Post-translational modifications

  • Removal of methionine and the signal peptide, partial proteolysis.
  • Phosphorylation, acetylation (histones), methylation.
  • Glycosylation, lipid attachment (membrane anchors).
  • Hydroxylation (vitamin C), γ-carboxylation (vitamin K), disulfide bond formation.
  • Ubiquitination — degradation in the proteasome.
